description:
CORRECTION, same session, after reading the snapshot's OWN header: this drift is ALREADY KNOWN.  s473t5d wrote on 2026-09-13 (baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv header, "Seventeen MORE files differ from the snapshot ... NOT MINE"): twelve of them read identically on a 2ff53f8d extraction (comp/use.t, op/coreamp.t, op/coresubs.t, op/inc.t, op/inccode.t, op/inccode-tie.t, run/fresh_perl.t, run/switchM.t, uni/method.t, io/iofile.t, io/pipe.t, io/open.t), four are the runner's three-way rows-unstable verdict (io/crlf_through.t, io/through.t, io/pvbm.t, uni/variables.t) and TWO are the #1651 HANGS (op/gv.t, uni/gv.t); #1710 and #1708 name io/open.t and run/switchM.t.  So the gv.t TIMEOUTs are #1651, not a new slowdown, and the bisect suggestion above is superseded by that task.

WHAT THIS TASK IS, THEREFORE: the "a row I did not move is not mine to re-bless" rule has now left the same ~10 files reported as movers by EVERY companion run for at least four sessions (s473t5d, s484d, s486c, this review), each session re-verifying them on an extraction at the cost of an hour.  Decide ONCE: an attribute-and-splice pass (one agent, one session) that bisects each of the twelve stable ones to its commit (or cites #1708/#1710/#1651 where a task already owns it) and splices perl-suite-run.tsv + perl-suite-fails.tsv + row-shortfall.tsv ROW BY ROW with the cause -- after which the companion's SNAPSHOT block is quiet again and a NEW mover is visible at a glance.  Until then every merge review pays the re-verification; the numbers above are that re-verification for 2026-09-17.

FILED s487 (Fable, 2026-09-17) from the s486c merge review.  The s484d/s486c batch's owed companion (`--all --quick --jobs 2`, re-run by Fable on the s486c tree while two agents shared the box) reported these movers; every one was then re-run `--jobs 1` on the s486c tree AND on a `git archive 2ac855aa` extraction of main (load < 1 for the gv.t pair).  All ten read the SAME on the extraction as on the s486c tree, so they are main's own drift since the snapshot was blessed, not the batch's.  Per the merge protocol ("a mover you did not cause is NOT spliced -- name its class") they are recorded here, unspliced.

THE TABLE (snapshot -> main extraction 2ac855aa):
  op/gv.t        135/56 DIFF      -> TIMEOUT 67/24   (serial, load 0.8; the s486c tree reads the same)
  uni/gv.t        59/29 DIFF      -> TIMEOUT 0/0     (the s486c full run once read 75/84 DIFF -- a file on the timeout edge)
  comp/use.t      42/45           -> 40/47           NEW rows: "no strict refs allows ver decl to enable subs", "no strict vars allows ver decl to enable subs"
  io/open.t      154/34           -> 152/36          NEW rows: "chmod fails with \0 in name (overload)", "open with nul in pathnames since 5.18 [perl #117265] (overload)"
  op/coresubs.t    1/1            -> 0/2
  run/switchM.t    2/3            -> 0/5
  op/inccode.t    13/28           -> 13/26           row-shortfall 48 -> 50
  op/inc.t        62/13           -> 67/26           row-shortfall 18 -> 0 (the file now produces every row)
  run/switches.t  28/112          -> 28/112          row-shortfall 11 -> 0
  op/coreamp.t     9/46           -> 9/58            NEW rows: "&caller with too many args", "effect of &CORE::close"; aborted-forms 15 -> 18; row-shortfall 723 -> 711
  (io/pvbm.t 23/5 read 21/7 and 20/8 under load and 23/5 serially -- the known load-flaky file, not listed.)

WHAT TO DO: for each file, bisect between the snapshot's bless commit and 2ac855aa (the s484c/s473t5f/s484a..s486b merges are the candidates -- s486b changed the registry marker in cl/pcl-test.lisp, but the companion never loads the registry), then either fix or splice `baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv` + `perl-suite-fails.tsv` + `row-shortfall.tsv` ROW BY ROW with the cause.  The gv.t pair is the one to take first: two files that used to COMPLETE now hit the clock at low load, which is a slowdown or a hang somewhere in glob handling (s484c's #1726/#1727 typeglob arms are the obvious suspects -- its own review measured +4.7 %/+12.3 % on element derefs before a fast arm was added).  Cheap discriminating measurement: `tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1 op/gv.t` on a `git archive` of the commit BEFORE s484c (f6b56feb) vs f74667ea.

ALSO FOUND, same review: `--bless-fails` / `--bless-shortfall` are WHOLE-FILE rewrites even for a one-file run -- see #1835.
=== DONE (s488a, 2026-09-17) ===
Every stable mover is attributed to ONE COMMIT, measured OLD at that commit's
immediate PARENT and NEW at the commit itself (`git archive` extraction,
`tools/run-perl-suite.pl --jobs 1`, the runner's own serial re-run agreeing);
`git rev-list --count PARENT..COMMIT` = 1 for every pair, so each answer is a
commit and not a window.  Fourteen probe points over five probe lists; the
instruments are kept in the worktree's `scratch/s488a/` (at-commit.sh, probe.sh,
probe-list*.txt, probes.txt, p-*.tsv).

  op/gv.t     135/56 DIFF -> TIMEOUT 67/24   0ea8d7e1  s473h m7 #1249(7)
  uni/gv.t    59/29 -> TIMEOUT 0/0           0ea8d7e1
  comp/use.t  42/45 -> 40/47                 0ea8d7e1
  run/switchM.t 2/3 -> 0/5                   ec8ac8c0  s473u m2 #1545
  run/fresh_perl.t 60/31 -> 61/30 (STALE)    6aa2f358  s473e m1 #1161/#1244(a)
  op/inc.t    62/13 -> 67/26, sf 18 -> 0     e2536f81  s473d m3 #1248(b)
  io/open.t   154/34 -> 152/36               4bdde171  s473w m4 #1507
  io/pipe.t   18/14 -> 19/13                 5fe48176  s473f m2 #1307/#1246
  io/iofile.t 1/2 -> 2/1                     a31369fc  s473f m5 #1074
  op/inccode.t 13/28 -> 13/26, sf 48 -> 50   319d0f4d  s483a m1 #1592
  op/coreamp.t 9/46 -> 9/58, sf 723 -> 711   4af36604  s484a m3 #1586
  op/coresubs.t 1/1 -> 0/2                   4af36604

THREE are not behaviour moves: run/switches.t's shortfall 11 was BOOKKEEPING
(the s473t5d splice wrote it beside its own verdict row of 28/112 = all 140 of
perl's rows); op/inccode-tie.t's fails ROWKEY was the message TEXT where the
runner projects a test#-0 row to `*summary*`; op/coreamp.t + op/coresubs.t are
CAPPED at 500 logged rows, so a row entering the log pushes another out.

NOT SPLICED: io/pvbm.t, the known flapper (23/5 alone, 20/8 in a batch â the
ninth recording).  The runner's `*rows-unstable*` gates the ROW check only and
the #366 three-way line is a LABEL, so a file whose COUNT flaps reports as a
SNAPSHOT mover forever: FILED as #1851 with the one mechanism proposed (a
per-file band in the snapshot, three serial runs as the entry bar).

SPLICED (commit d4cc28a6, row by row, the diff read before committing):
perl-suite-run.tsv 12 verdict rows + a header block carrying the table and the
resolution of the s473t5d "Seventeen MORE files â¦ NOT MINE" paragraph;
perl-suite-fails.tsv 9 added / 5 removed / 1 rowkey repaired;
row-shortfall.tsv 4 rows; perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv 1 stale registration
removed.  `tools/cause-census.pl --hygiene` clean.

ALSO FILED: #1850 â `$| = 1` does not make PCL's writes immediate (0 bytes
mid-run where perl writes 273, for a bare print, `print STDOUT` and the select
idiom; no flush on SIGTERM/SIGKILL).  It is the instrument blocker behind
#1651, which got the whole member-2 measurement appended (the hang STARTS at
0ea8d7e1 and is NOT the runperl child at gv.t:321).
